questions.question: How does the brightness of two bulbs connected in parallel compare to two of the same bulbs connected in series using the same battery?
options: The bulbs in parallel are brighter than the bulbs in series.
The bulbs in series are brighter than the bulbs in parallel.
Both sets of bulbs have exactly the same brightness.
The bulbs in parallel do not light up at all.

questions.question: If you connect two identical bulbs to a battery, how does the current flowing through them in a parallel circuit compare to a series circuit?
options: The current through the parallel bulbs is smaller than through the series bulbs.
The current through the parallel bulbs is bigger than through the series bulbs.
The current is exactly the same in both circuits.
No current flows through the parallel bulbs.

questions.question: When comparing two identical bulbs connected to the same battery, what is true about the voltage across one of the bulbs in parallel compared to one in series?
options: The voltage across one bulb in parallel is smaller than across one bulb in series.
The voltage across one bulb in parallel is bigger than across one bulb in series.
The voltage is exactly the same across both bulbs in both setups.
There is zero voltage across a bulb connected in parallel.

questions.question: What will happen to a battery lighting two bulbs in parallel compared to the same battery lighting two bulbs in series?
options: The battery lighting the parallel bulbs will run out faster.
The battery lighting the series bulbs will run out faster.
Both batteries will run out at exactly the same time.
The battery lighting the parallel bulbs will last forever.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly identifies what an ammeter measures and its units?
options: Voltage in volts (V)
Resistance in ohms (Ω)
Current in amps (A)
Power in watts (W)

questions.question: In physics, what is electrical resistance a measure of?
options: How difficult it is for an electrical current to flow.
The amount of energy stored within a battery.
The speed at which electrons travel through empty space.
The total number of loops in a parallel circuit.

questions.question: What is the unit of measurement for electrical resistance?
options: Amps (A)
Volts (V)
Ohms (Ω)
Watts (W)

questions.question: How does changing the length of a wire affect its electrical resistance?
options: The longer the wire, the greater its resistance.
The longer the wire, the smaller its resistance.
Wire length has no effect on its resistance.
Longer wires have zero resistance.

questions.question: If you double the length of a wire, what happens to its electrical resistance?
options: Its resistance is halved.
Its resistance doubles.
Its resistance becomes four times greater.
Its resistance remains unchanged.

questions.question: What is the relationship between the resistance of a uniform wire and its length?
options: Resistance is inversely proportional to its length.
Resistance is proportional to its length.
Resistance is equal to the square of its length.
Resistance is completely independent of its length.

questions.question: What unit is used to measure electrical power?
options: Volts (V)
Amps (A)
Ohms (Ω)
Watts (W)

questions.question: How is the energy used by an electrical device calculated in kilowatt-hours (kWh)?
options: Multiplying power in kilowatts (kW) by time in hours (h).
Dividing power in kilowatts (kW) by time in hours (h).
Multiplying resistance in ohms (Ω) by current in amps (A).
Dividing voltage in volts (V) by power in watts (W).

questions.question: Which of the following describes a parallel circuit?
options: A single loop circuit with only one path for the current.
A circuit with more than one complete loop from one end of a battery to the other.
A circuit that does not require a battery or power source to function.
A circuit where the wire is drawn with gaps to stop the current.

questions.question: How does the current through each branch of a parallel circuit relate to the total current?
options: The current through each branch adds up to the total current through the battery.
The current through each branch is always double the total current through the battery.
The current through each branch is completely independent of the battery's current.
The total current through the battery is divided by the number of branches squared.

questions.question: What is the relationship between the thickness of a wire and its resistance?
options: The thicker the wire, the smaller its resistance.
The thicker the wire, the greater its resistance.
The thickness of a wire does not affect its resistance.
Thicker wires have infinite resistance.

questions.question: What happens to the electrical resistance of a wire if its cross-sectional area is doubled?
options: Its resistance is doubled.
Its resistance is halved.
Its resistance increases four times.
Its resistance remains exactly the same.

questions.question: How does the voltage across each branch of a parallel circuit compare to the voltage of the battery?
options: It is the same as the voltage across the cell or battery.
It is divided equally among the different branches.
It is always zero across every branch.
It is double the voltage across the cell or battery.
